transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marcus Reed (Redwood); Samir Patel, Dana Liu, Marko Vasic (AureliaSearch)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on this motion, and Marcus our solutions engineer is here. Samir, thanks for setting this up.
[00:05] Samir: Yep, thanks. We wanted to see how your hosted API could help our relevance problems — current results are noisy for long-tail queries.
[00:12] Marcus: Cool, we'll walk through embeddings and our rerank endpoint, show the console and Optimize suggestions. Quick qual: what's your current vector store and latency SLA?
[00:20] Dana: We're using an in-house FAISS cluster + some caching, 200ms p95 on average but spikes to 400-500ms during peak. We need p95 under 300ms for search queries.
[00:33] Marko: Also need to understand data residency — some logs can't leave EU.
[00:38] Marcus: Totally. On hosted we have region controls and options for dedicated pods if you need stronger isolation. For the demo we'll show hosted EU region and also touch on Dedicated and Private later.
[00:48] Lena: Quick agenda: 1) embeddings endpoint, 2) negation/hard match pitfalls, 3) rerank endpoint demo with a hybrid search + rerank flow, 4) console + Optimize recommendations, 5) next steps.
[01:05] Dana: Sounds good.

--- Embeddings endpoint walkthrough ---
[01:18] Marcus: API first — you call /v1/embeddings with text and get a 1536-d float vector (or model depending). Example: POST /v1/embeddings body { 'model': 'redwood-embed-2', 'input': 'how to reset my password' } returns vector.
[01:36] Samir: Are vectors normalized? We currently normalize on ingest.
[01:40] Marcus: We return raw vectors but recommend storing normalized if your similarity uses dot product; we also provide cosine helpers in the SDKs.
[01:48] Marcus: Performance-wise hosted embeddings is sub 10ms median per call for small payloads in EU region; batching helps if you bulk index.
[01:57] Dana: Does Redwood manage the vector store or do you expect customers to bring their own?
[02:02] Marcus: We support both. For the rerank flow we typically do a hybrid: external ANN for candidate generation (Pinecone/FAISS), then call Redwood rerank to score top-k. For customers who prefer one-stop, we have integrations and docs for embedding + lightweight storage, but many teams keep their own ANN.
[02:20] Marko: How do you handle stale KV cache or prefix caching? I heard about KV cash in your blog but not clear.
[02:27] Marcus: Haha KV cash — yes, KV cache for autoregressive models. For embeddings/rerank it's less relevant; caching applies to prefix caching for chat. For rerank we do per-request caching of past rerank results if you enable cache TTLs in the console.

--- Rerank endpoint demo ---
[02:45] Marcus: Ok demo. We'll run a sample pipeline: user query -> ANN top 100 -> rerank top 10 with Redwood. I'll share a live request.
[02:55] (screen share begins)
[03:05] Marcus: Here in the Console you can see the Rerank API settings: model selection, temperature(0 — deterministic), soft vs hard scoring, and an option for 'preserve original rank if confidence low'.
[03:19] Lena: For search relevance this 'preserve original rank' is handy to avoid reranker regressions on short queries.
[03:26] Dana: How do you compute confidence? Is that based on score delta or model calibration?
[03:31] Marcus: It's a heuristic — score delta + learned threshold per query distribution. Optimize can suggest thresholds based on your eval set.
[03:38] Marcus: Running example: query 'return policy international orders' — ANN returned 100 candidates. We send top 10 ids with their context to /v1/rerank.
[03:48] (typing)
[03:53] Marcus: Response back in 120ms — new ranked list with scores.
[03:56] Samir: 120ms from cloud endpoint is fine, but our overall pipeline includes network + ANN lookup, so total p95 is our concern.
[04:06] Marcus: Right, locally we see rerank p95 around 80-150ms depending on input length and model. We also have a 'low-latency' rerank flavor that uses smaller model sizes for under 50ms at lower cost.
[04:18] Dana: Can we configure per-route model selection? For example search gets low-latency, help center gets high-precision.
[04:24] Lena: Yes, per-route model config in Console or API routes. You can pin different models per route and set fallbacks.

--- Console + Optimize ---
[04:35] Marcus: Switching to Optimize — this page ingests query logs and evaluation sets and suggests batching, quantization, and model choices. For example, it recommended quantizing your rerank model to int8 for 2-3x cost improvement with minimal quality loss on similar workloads.
[04:52] Dana: We care about deterministic outputs for rerank, quantization noise worries me.
[04:57] Marcus: Optimize runs regressions on your eval set and flags potential quality drop. You can require a threshold before applying quantization in production.
[05:07] Samir: About costs — how do hosted per-token + rerank charges compare to running everything on our FAISS cluster?
[05:14] Lena: Good question. For many customers, the unit economics favor hosted for small-to-medium scale because we amortize infra and have intelligent batching/caching. For very high QPS, Dedicated reserved capacity is usually cheaper. We'll send a model vs dedicated cost sheet.

--- Security and compliance ---
[05:30] Samir: Quick security checks: SOC 2, encryption at rest, KMS integration, SSO?
[05:36] Lena: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated options, SSO via SAML, RBAC in Console, audit logs. We're happy to share the security pack.
[05:48] Marko: For data residency — can we ensure embeddings derived from EU data never leave region?
[05:53] Marcus: For hosted EU region we store and process in EU; for stricter needs we recommend Private or Dedicated in your VPC. We'll include a data residency addendum in materials.

--- Technical deep dive — tuning reranker ---
[06:05] Dana: On the reranker model inputs — do you provide token limits, truncation strategies? Sometimes our contexts are long.
[06:12] Marcus: Rerank accepts short contexts per candidate; we provide strategies to summarize or highlight candidate snippets. For long contexts we recommend a hybrid approach: compress with intent-extraction embedding + candidate snippets, or use a two-pass pipeline.
[06:25] Dana: For our logs, we have 150 tokens average snippet length, sometimes 800.
[06:30] Marcus: Ok, Optimize will flag high-length items and suggest compression templates.
[06:35] Samir: Any network considerations for bringing ANN and rerank closer?
[06:38] Marcus: Co-locating ANN in same cloud region reduces latency. For Dedicated you can run both within same VPC for sub-10ms internal calls depending on topology.

--- Objections and tradeoffs ---
[06:50] Marko: Concern: if we move to hosted rerank, debugging and explainability of ranking changes is harder.
[06:56] Lena: We expose per-request scoring breakdowns in the Console and can log intermediate features. Also you can run local offline rerank with model we provide for parity checks.
[07:07] Dana: Are model weights downloadable? We need to run offline A/B tests internally.
[07:11] Marcus: For open models we provide model bundles for Private deployments; for hosted we provide a parity harness but weights are not downloadable for Redwood-managed models unless on Private.

--- Live benchmark idea ---
[07:23] Lena: Proposal: we run a 2-week POC. You send a 10k query eval set, we run rerank vs your baseline, produce NDCG and latency metrics, and a regression dashboard.
[07:34] Samir: That sounds good. Timeline: we need initial results for vendor review by March 25.
[07:40] Lena: We can meet that if Dana shares logs by Friday.

--- Closing and recap ---
[07:48] Lena: Recap — we'll send pricing and security docs, Marcus will send benchmark scripts, Dana will share sample logs and eval set. We'll schedule POC kickoff and put success criteria in CR.
[07:58] Samir: Great, thanks.
[08:00] Marcus: One last note — for rerank costs, you can dial model size per route and set fallback to a cheaper variant during spikes.
[08:08] Marko: Good to know.
[08:12] Lena: Ok we'll follow up via email. Thanks all.
[08:16] Samir: Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional ASR substitutions (KV cash, Redwood Dedicated pronounced slightly) and generic speaker labels in some segments.
questions: Can Redwood guarantee EU-only processing for hosted?
How much latency does rerank add in typical hybrid flow?
Will Redwood provide a parity harness for offline A/B?
